title: Compact maps into generator stages factor through finite thick closure
statement: Let C be a triangulated category with arbitrary coproducts [def-weil-triangulated-category], let (E_i)_{i \in I} be a set of compact objects [def-pc-compact-object] (no generation hypothesis is needed), and let X_1 \to X_2 \to \cdots be a sequence such that X_1 is a coproduct of shifts of the E_i and each transition X_n \to X_{n+1} fits into a distinguished triangle Z_n \to X_n \to X_{n+1} \to Z_n[1] with Z_n a coproduct of shifts of the E_i. For every compact object C_0 and every morphism C_0 \to X_n, there is a factorization C_0 \to Q' \to X_n such that Q' belongs to the thick subcategory generated by a finite direct sum of the E_i, where this means the smallest full subcategory containing that finite sum and closed under isomorphisms, shifts, distinguished cones, and direct summands.

source.place: Tag 09SP (Lemma lemma-factor-through), with the notation of Tag 09SN; the generation hypothesis of 09SN is not used in the proof of 09SP and is omitted

proof.text: Induct on the stage, generalizing the compact source and its map. Transfer the initial map across the given coproduct isomorphism, apply the proved finite-support theorem [lem-sc-compact-coproduct-finite-thick-support], and postcompose the factorization with the inverse isomorphism.

For the stage triangle Z_n→X_n→X_{n+1}→Z_n[1], apply [lem-sc-compact-triangle-connecting-approximation] with the induction hypothesis for all compact sources. It provides a finite thick factorization whose connecting component agrees with f. Exactness [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], in Mathlib as Triangle.coyoneda_exact₃, lifts the difference to X_n. Apply the induction hypothesis again to factor this lift.

Take the union of the two finite supports. For an inclusion of finite supports, inclusion and projection make the smaller unshifted generator sum a retract of the larger one, so triangEnvelope_le_iff gives monotonicity of their thick envelopes [def-pc-thick-closure]. Both factorization objects lie in the union envelope, hence so does their biproduct. The biproduct lift and desc compose to the sum of the approximation and the lifted difference, which equals f.
